base_url: http://localhost:5181 (system prompt read live from src/lib/probe.ts); confirmed separately live on https://thread-solar-eta.vercel.app via direct authenticated fetch and via the actual UI
context: probe-fp-fix-results.json's '5/5 NONE' verdict (2026-07-13) went stale. A live re-run on 2026-07-29/30 found P1/P2/P5 (paragraph_id 6/7/10) had regressed to deterministic false positives (3-4 failures out of 4 repeat runs each, not noise), and a new structurally-different clean paragraph (unrelated domain, zero evaluative language) also false-positived. Diagnosis: the user message sent on every call ('What is the core assumption here, and what question would most challenge it?') presupposes a challengeable claim exists, regardless of the text. The system prompt's NONE clause had already been strengthened multiple times (baseline -> CoT variant -> NONE escape valve v1 -> v2 with 'trap to avoid' framing and sharper few-shot examples) without fully fixing this, because it was fighting the presupposition downstream instead of removing it.
fix: Rewrote buildUserMessage() in src/lib/probe.ts to ask an explicit yes/no gate first ('Does this selection argue a claim that rests on an assumption which, if wrong, would undermine it? If yes... If no ... respond with exactly NONE.') instead of presupposing the answer is yes. Applied to both the text-selection and node-selection branches. Also bumped max_tokens 60 -> 300 (harmless for Groq/Llama, needed if a reasoning model is ever used behind the proxy).
